part1_theory.json.old: Chapter 2 of the source book is the main organizing source, especially Sections 2.1 on spatial models, 2.2 on representation modes, 2.3 on object collections and 2.4 on data exchange [1].
part1_theory.json.new: Chapter 2 “Representation of Spatial Objects” of Spatial Databases: With Application to GIS is the main organizing source [1, pp. 29–67]. Section 2.1 “Geographic Space Modeling” distinguishes entity and field models (pp. 31–34); Section 2.2 “Representation Modes” introduces tessellation, vector and half-planes (pp. 35–46); Section 2.3 “Representing the Geometry of a Collection of Objects” presents spaghetti, network and topology (pp. 46–51). Section 2.4 “Spatial Data Formats and Exchange Standards” has the TIGER/Line example (pp. 51–64); Section 2.5 contains the bibliographic notes (pp. 64–67).
